data.narrative:
1872 is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Dan Summers that has raised $15M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a broader Robotics & Manufacturing sector universe of 9 private peers and 1 public comparable (277810.KQ), though tighter peer filtering yielded insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage datapoints for reliable median-based triangulation.

The stage-progression method applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage advancement, using the $15M total raised as a proxy baseline. This yields an implied valuation of $38M. A peer-median approach was not applicable due to insufficient narrow-filter comparables within the robotics sector at similar stage and valuation tier; the identified private peers (Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Bedrock Robotics, and others) span wider stage and scale distributions that would produce misleading central estimates.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $32M to $43M, with a median of $38M, derived from the single applicable method. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the 2.5x multiplier for this specific company's growth trajectory, the absence of tightly-matched peer benchmarks, and the limited data on 1872's unit economics relative to the broader sector. This range should be updated as additional comparable funding events emerge in the robotics space.
